object_context: Child of YM-E1a for RAKL_math issue #5: determine whether one exact Balaban-style renormalization-group blocking step for four-dimensional pure lattice Yang–Mills can carry a deliberately small finite family of positive-half-space gauge-invariant source insertions through an explicit marked/source sector with controlled operator mixing, bounded support enlargement, reflection-compatible placement, and source-derivative estimates that do not already incur ultraviolet-depth-dependent loss.
structural_coordinates: the underlying unmarked object is one exact gauge-covariant lattice RG blocking step in four-dimensional pure non-Abelian Yang–Mills
the mark is a finite source vector coupled only to gauge-invariant cutoff observables; derivatives at zero source encode connected insertions rather than a new physical interaction
one-step exact differentiation gives a transport identity, but useful closure additionally requires a controlled representation of the resulting coarse observable/source dependence
operator/source mixing can enlarge the marked basis even when the unmarked effective density remains in a controlled RG class
Wilson-loop and loop-cylinder insertions are bounded and exactly gauge invariant at fixed cutoff, but blocking can change contour geometry and generate multi-loop or extended-support terms

reflection positivity is a property of a positive-half-space algebra and reflected quadratic forms; an RG block or source support that straddles the reflection plane can invalidate naive positivity transport
finite source closure is only a calibration target and must not be confused with a separating continuum observable algebra or spectral completeness
scale-neutral one-step constants are necessary but not sufficient for multiscale summability; any per-step loss must be tracked against the asymptotically-free running coupling and number of RG steps
continuum existence, non-triviality, OS reconstruction, infinite-volume passage, correlation decay and mass gap remain downstream obligations
equivalent_formulations: differentiate a normalized source-dependent block integral at J=0 and ask whether the conditional expectation of each fine observable belongs to a controlled coarse marked-observable class with an explicit remainder bound

construct a one-step source-mixing matrix plus controlled irrelevant remainder for a finite gauge-invariant observable family, with support and norm budgets bound independently of total ultraviolet depth

show that the tangent map of the RG transformation in selected gauge-invariant source directions is a bounded map between explicitly defined marked Banach spaces, with a reflection-compatible source cone on supported observables
falsify finite marked closure by exhibiting unavoidable operator-basis or support proliferation after one exact blocking step
solved_analogues: Osterwalder–Seiler 1978 fixed-cutoff Wilson lattice gauge theory: reflection positivity and positive transfer-matrix structure for the regulator-level theory

Brydges–Fröhlich–Seiler 1979 constructive lattice gauge/Higgs analysis: gauge invariance and Osterwalder–Schrader positivity can be controlled uniformly in lattice spacing in lower-dimensional/superrenormalizable gauge settings
near_solved_analogues: Balaban 1987–1989 four-dimensional pure lattice gauge RG: localized effective actions, coupling renormalization, cluster expansions and large-field control for the unmarked theory, without a source-insertion closure theorem sufficient for continuum observable construction

Magnen–Rivasseau–Sénéor 1993 pure SU(2) YM4 with fixed infrared cutoff and no ultraviolet cutoff: rigorous Schwinger-function construction in a regularized axial gauge with nonperturbative restoration of Slavnov identities, but not the full Clay theory
Brandt–Neri–Sato 1981 perturbative Wilson-loop renormalization: loop insertions close only after geometry-dependent renormalization data including cusp/intersection structure

method_transfers.source_context: Balaban one-step lattice gauge renormalization group
method_transfers.method: differentiate the exact block transformation in a finite set of source directions and represent the source tangent/remainder in a marked norm built on the same localization and small/large-field decomposition as the unmarked RG
shared_structure: same four-dimensional pure lattice gauge setting and asymptotically-free ultraviolet trajectory
same exact scale-by-scale block transformation and localized effective-density machinery
same need for estimates uniform across an increasing number of ultraviolet steps
required_assumptions: source differentiation is justified under the finite-cutoff block integral
generated insertions admit a localized gauge-invariant expansion compatible with the unmarked polymer/cluster organization
mixing and support growth can be bounded in a norm whose one-step constant does not accumulate catastrophically
disanalogies: Balaban's unmarked stability does not itself control tangent directions corresponding to observable insertions
marked insertions can introduce new local/nonlocal structures, mixing coefficients and support growth absent from the normalization sector
method_transfers.repair_question: For the smallest Wilson-loop/cylinder source family, what exact marked state space makes the differentiated one-step map closed up to a quantitatively controlled remainder, and what is the first generated term that violates that space if no such closure holds?

method_transfers.method: align the reflection plane and block decomposition, restrict calibration sources to a buffered positive-half-space algebra, and require any proposed source-mixing/support map to preserve a finite reflected Gram-cone test before multiscale iteration
shared_structure: same Wilson regulator and compact gauge group
reflection positivity is expressible as finite quadratic-form inequalities at each cutoff
required_assumptions: the RG blocking kernel and source embedding respect the chosen reflection geometry
coarse representatives of supported sources remain in the positive-half-space algebra or have a quantitatively controlled buffer that never crosses the reflection plane
disanalogies: fixed-cutoff positivity does not imply that an arbitrary coarse-graining map preserves the positive-half-space support algebra
source renormalization/mixing may create extended terms not covered by the original reflected observable set
method_transfers.repair_question: Can the first marked RG calibration be arranged on blocks strictly separated from the reflection plane so that reflected Gram positivity is an exact finite-cutoff invariant, or does unavoidable support leakage appear after one step?
source_anchors: K. Osterwalder and E. Seiler, Gauge field theories on a lattice, Ann. Phys. 110 (1978) 440–471, DOI:10.1016/0003-4916(78)90039-8

method_transfers.method: treat loop geometry and its renormalization labels as part of the marked state rather than assuming a single scalar source coefficient follows a contour unchanged under blocking
shared_structure: gauge-invariant loop observables are the selected fixed-cutoff calibration sources
renormalization of loop observables depends on local geometric singularities and intersections
required_assumptions: the block/refinement map supplies a consistent physical-contour identification
the marked basis records enough contour and intersection data for generated loop structures to be represented or quantitatively remainder-controlled
disanalogies: the source result is perturbative continuum loop renormalization rather than a nonperturbative exact lattice RG closure theorem
one RG block can generate multi-loop/polymer structures beyond a single loop renormalization matrix
method_transfers.repair_question: What minimum geometry/multi-loop labels must be added before one-step Wilson-source transport ceases to leak outside the registered marked basis?

method_transfers.source_context: Magnen–Rivasseau–Sénéor YM4 with an infrared cutoff
method_transfers.method: use source/Schwinger-function control and nonperturbative gauge-identity restoration as a contrastive model for keeping observable information explicit through ultraviolet removal
shared_structure: four-dimensional pure non-Abelian Yang–Mills ultraviolet problem
Schwinger functions rather than partition-function bounds are the observable target
gauge invariance must survive or return after regulator-dependent intermediate representations
required_assumptions: the lattice RG source sector has an analogue of the controlled counterterm/gauge-identity bookkeeping used in the axial-gauge construction

disanalogies: the construction is SU(2), fixed infrared cutoff and trivial topological sector in a regularized axial gauge

explicit_disanalogies: an exact source derivative identity is not a source-closure theorem
finite-dimensional closure for one hand-picked source family is not a separating observable algebra
one-step boundedness is not multiscale uniformity
reflection positivity of the underlying Wilson measure is not automatic positivity preservation under arbitrary source mixing or support enlargement
perturbative loop renormalizability does not prove nonperturbative marked RG closure
fixed-infrared-cutoff SU(2) ultraviolet construction does not supply arbitrary compact simple gauge group, infinite-volume, or mass-gap closure

the sibling spectral source-visibility failure warns that restricted source families can miss physical states; this child uses a finite family only as a closure calibration and makes no spectral-completeness claim

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A compiler pass can preserve the uninstrumented program semantics while an attached finite instrumentation vocabulary explodes into new data-flow facts, aliases or dependencies; useful instrumentation therefore needs an explicit transfer function, a closure domain and a widening/error budget.
common_abstraction: a base transformation can be stable while marked observables are not closed under it
a finite mark vocabulary may proliferate under one transformation
support/dependency growth and approximation error must be budgeted before repeated composition
source_to_target_mapping: compiler pass -> one RG blocking step
instrumented variables/data-flow facts -> gauge-invariant source insertions
abstract domain -> marked observable/source Banach space
alias/dependency growth -> operator mixing and support enlargement
widening/error budget -> controlled irrelevant remainder and one-step norm loss
shared_constraints: the marked state must be transported explicitly rather than inferred after the base transformation
closure must be tested after one step before iterating many steps
unbounded vocabulary/support growth makes repeated composition unusable
disanalogies: compiler instrumentation is discrete and deterministic, while RG integrates fluctuating gauge degrees of freedom
Yang–Mills insertions carry ultraviolet singularities, gauge geometry and reflection-positivity constraints with no software analogue
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Before attempting multiscale marked RG, define the smallest marked source space and measure one-step basis/support/norm growth; if exact finite closure fails, widen only to the minimal graded/quasi-local space justified by the observed leakage.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: For a finite Wilson-loop/cylinder source family, derive the exact finite-cutoff source derivative after one registered blocking step and either express it in the proposed marked space with explicit remainder/support/norm bounds or exhibit the first generated term that violates closure.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Proposal compressor only; no gauge-theory statement follows from the software analogy.
